# Spiral Design Report: Aerial Survey Aircraft

**Status:** Converged after **2** spiral laps.

## Summary
A high-aspect-ratio aerial survey aircraft with a 1,200 km range and an aspect ratio of 13.5 was sized around a 7075-T6 aluminium wing spar. The design spiral converged in 2 laps with a 0.14% MTOW change from the first to the last lap. The final configuration has a maximum takeoff weight (MTOW) of 1,369.0 kg, an empty mass of 764.5 kg, and a beam-theory spar mass of 65.8 kg (4.8% of MTOW) sized to a 0.0 safety margin at 434.4 MPa.

_Narrative paragraphs written by Gemini (gemini-4-argon) from the computed results below; every number in them was checked against the design state._

## Mission & configuration
- **Range:** 1,200 km with 45 min reserve
- **Cruise:** 60.0 m/s at 2,500 m
- **Stall speed:** 28.0 m/s
- **Payload:** 1 crew + 3 passengers at 86.0 kg, 50.0 kg baggage (394.0 kg payload)
- **Wing:** high wing, aspect ratio 13.5, taper ratio 0.45, t/c 0.15, CL_max 1.6, L/D_max 11
- **Propulsion:** propeller efficiency 0.8, BSFC 6.80e-08 kg/J
- **Structure:** +3.8 g limit x 1.5 = 5.70 g ultimate, spar material `al_7075_t6`

## Convergence history
| Lap | MTOW (kg) | ΔMTOW (%) | Empty (kg) | Fuel (kg) | Spar (kg) | Wing area (m²) | Span (m) | Peak bending stress (MPa) | Tip deflection (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1,367.1 | n/a | 762.9 | 210.2 | 65.7 | 17.45 | 15.35 | 434.4 | 2,084.9 |
| 1 | 1,369.0 | +0.14 | 764.5 | 210.5 | 65.8 | 17.47 | 15.36 | 434.4 | 2,087.1 |

## Mass breakdown
- **MTOW:** 1,369.0 kg
- **Empty mass:** 764.5 kg (empty fraction 0.558)
- **Fuel mass:** 210.5 kg (fuel fraction 0.154)
- **Payload:** 394.0 kg
- **Spar mass used in sizing:** 65.7 kg (statistical estimate 64.9 kg)

| Item | Mass (kg) | Share of MTOW (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Wing spar (both wings) | 65.7 | 4.8 |
| Rest of empty mass | 698.8 | 51.0 |
| Fuel | 210.5 | 15.4 |
| Crew | 86.0 | 6.3 |
| Passengers | 258.0 | 18.8 |
| Baggage | 50.0 | 3.7 |

## Wing & power
- **Wing area / span:** 17.47 m² / 15.36 m (wing loading 768 Pa)
- **Root / tip chord / MAC:** 1.57 m / 0.71 m / 1.19 m
- **Cruise / installed power:** 91.5 kW / 157.5 kW

## Main wing spar (beam theory)
- **Material:** `al_7075_t6`
- **Spar mass:** 65.8 kg both wings (32.9 kg per wing)
- **Root / tip depth:** 200.0 mm / 90.0 mm
- **Root cap:** 70.0 mm wide x 26.97 mm thick; web 2.82 mm
- **Peak bending stress:** 434.4 MPa against 434.4 MPa allowable (margin +0.00)
- **Peak shear stress:** 67.7 MPa
- **Tip deflection at 5.70 g ultimate:** 2,087.1 mm

## FEA vs beam theory
Solver: Timoshenko beam FEA (NumPy direct stiffness)

| Quantity | FEA | Beam theory | Agreement (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Peak stress (MPa) | 437.2 | 434.4 | 99.4 |
| Tip deflection (mm) | 2,092.3 | 2,087.1 | 99.8 |

FEA safety margin: -0.01

## Discussion
### What drove the design
The 1,200.0 km range and 45.0 min loiter reserve, flown at 60.0 m/s with an assumed L/D max of 11.0 (Raymer 2ed, Ch. 3 (p. 22)), require 210.5 kg of fuel (15.4% of MTOW) alongside the 394.0 kg payload (1 crew and 3 passengers at 86.0 kg each, plus 50.0 kg baggage). The 28.0 m/s stall speed and maximum lift coefficient of 1.6 set the wing loading at 768.0 Pa and wing area at 17.47 m2, which at an aspect ratio of 13.5 produces a 15.36 m span; note that this aspect ratio is outside the typical single-engine range of 6 to 10. Structural sizing of the 7075-T6 spar (Converted to SI from Raymer 2ed, Table 14.3 (p. 366), row Clad 7075-T6 sheet) is driven by the 5.7 g ultimate load factor (3.8 g limit with a 1.5 ultimate factor) and a 0.15 thickness-to-chord ratio, with web shear buckling governing web thickness at 14 of 21 spanwise stations.

### Trade-offs
The sized beam-theory spar mass of 65.8 kg (65.7 kg used in sizing) is very close to the initial statistical estimate of 64.9 kg, even with the high 13.5 aspect ratio and a 2,087.1 mm tip deflection under ultimate load. Because the caps are sized directly to the 434.4 MPa allowable stress (Raymer 2ed, Eq. 14.35 (p. 383)), the analytical safety margin is 0.0, though the model omits inertia relief and crippling. Verification with Timoshenko beam FEA (NumPy direct stiffness) shows a 99.4% stress agreement and 99.8% deflection agreement, predicting a slightly higher peak von Mises stress of 437.2 MPa and 2,092.3 mm tip deflection, which results in a -0.01 FEA safety margin.

## Assumptions
- Cruise at L/D max = 11; loiter at 0.866 L/D max (Raymer 2ed, Ch. 3 (p. 22))
- Loiter speed = 0.75 x cruise speed
- Spar = 8.5% of statistical empty weight on lap 0 (Assumption (Spiral): not from a textbook table)
- Cruise flown at 75% of installed power
- Stall wing loading at ISA sea-level density (1.225 kg/m^3)
- Ultimate manoeuvring load factor n_ult = 5.70
- Cantilever wing root at y = 0 m; aero lift carried 100% by main spar
- No inertia relief from wing structure or fuel (conservative)
- Ultimate load = 1.5 x limit load (Raymer 2ed, p. 335)
- Spar depth = 85% of local aerofoil thickness; cap width = 35% of depth
- Caps sized at ultimate load to compression yield F_cy = 434 MPa (compression cap governs; crippling not modelled)
- Tension cap margin against F_tu = 496 MPa: +0.14
- Web: no shear failure (F_su = 296 MPa) and no shear buckling, unstiffened panel, K = 4.8 (classical long simply supported panel; Raymer gives K as a chart, Fig. 14.42)
- Minimum gauges: cap >= 2.0 mm, web >= 1.5 mm (assumption)
- Mass counts caps and web only: no stiffeners, ribs or fittings
- Tail moment arm = 52% of fuselage length (Raymer 2ed Table 6.4 typical arm ratio)
- Wing configuration: high wing
- Lofted 12-vertex tapered I-beam across 21 spanwise stations (y = 0 to 7.68 m)
- Includes 1.38x structural non-optimum mass factor for root carry-through fittings and web stiffeners
- Clamped root boundary condition (w = 0, dw/dy = 0) at wing root y = 0 m
- Timoshenko shear deformation factor Phi_e = 12*E*I / (G*A_web*L_e^2) per tapered element
- 3D von Mises stress recovery across outer flange fiber, web-flange fillet, and neutral axis

## Warnings
- aspect_ratio=13.5 is outside the typical GA single-engine range [6, 10] (Raymer 2ed, Table 4.1 (p. 51))
- Web shear buckling sets the web thickness at 14 of 21 stations

## Discussion
### What drove the design
The 1,200.0 km range and 45.0 min loiter reserve, flown at 60.0 m/s with an assumed L/D max of 11.0 (Raymer 2ed, Ch. 3 (p. 22)), require 210.5 kg of fuel (15.4% of MTOW) alongside the 394.0 kg payload (1 crew and 3 passengers at 86.0 kg each, plus 50.0 kg baggage). The 28.0 m/s stall speed and maximum lift coefficient of 1.6 set the wing loading at 768.0 Pa and wing area at 17.47 m2, which at an aspect ratio of 13.5 produces a 15.36 m span; note that this aspect ratio is outside the typical single-engine range of 6 to 10. Structural sizing of the 7075-T6 spar (Converted to SI from Raymer 2ed, Table 14.3 (p. 366), row Clad 7075-T6 sheet) is driven by the 5.7 g ultimate load factor (3.8 g limit with a 1.5 ultimate factor) and a 0.15 thickness-to-chord ratio, with web shear buckling governing web thickness at 14 of 21 spanwise stations.

### Trade-offs
The sized beam-theory spar mass of 65.8 kg (65.7 kg used in sizing) is very close to the initial statistical estimate of 64.9 kg, even with the high 13.5 aspect ratio and a 2,087.1 mm tip deflection under ultimate load. Because the caps are sized directly to the 434.4 MPa allowable stress (Raymer 2ed, Eq. 14.35 (p. 383)), the analytical safety margin is 0.0, though the model omits inertia relief and crippling. Verification with Timoshenko beam FEA (NumPy direct stiffness) shows a 99.4% stress agreement and 99.8% deflection agreement, predicting a slightly higher peak von Mises stress of 437.2 MPa and 2,092.3 mm tip deflection, which results in a -0.01 FEA safety margin.

## Assumptions
- Cruise at L/D max = 11; loiter at 0.866 L/D max (Raymer 2ed, Ch. 3 (p. 22))
- Loiter speed = 0.75 x cruise speed
- Spar = 8.5% of statistical empty weight on lap 0 (Assumption (Spiral): not from a textbook table)
- Cruise flown at 75% of installed power
- Stall wing loading at ISA sea-level density (1.225 kg/m^3)
- Ultimate manoeuvring load factor n_ult = 5.70
- Cantilever wing root at y = 0 m; aero lift carried 100% by main spar
- No inertia relief from wing structure or fuel (conservative)
- Ultimate load = 1.5 x limit load (Raymer 2ed, p. 335)
- Spar depth = 85% of local aerofoil thickness; cap width = 35% of depth
- Caps sized at ultimate load to compression yield F_cy = 434 MPa (compression cap governs; crippling not modelled)
- Tension cap margin against F_tu = 496 MPa: +0.14
- Web: no shear failure (F_su = 296 MPa) and no shear buckling, unstiffened panel, K = 4.8 (classical long simply supported panel; Raymer gives K as a chart, Fig. 14.42)
- Minimum gauges: cap >= 2.0 mm, web >= 1.5 mm (assumption)
- Mass counts caps and web only: no stiffeners, ribs or fittings
- Tail moment arm = 52% of fuselage length (Raymer 2ed Table 6.4 typical arm ratio)
- Wing configuration: high wing
- Lofted 12-vertex tapered I-beam across 21 spanwise stations (y = 0 to 7.68 m)
- Includes 1.38x structural non-optimum mass factor for root carry-through fittings and web stiffeners
- Clamped root boundary condition (w = 0, dw/dy = 0) at wing root y = 0 m
- Timoshenko shear deformation factor Phi_e = 12*E*I / (G*A_web*L_e^2) per tapered element
- 3D von Mises stress recovery across outer flange fiber, web-flange fillet, and neutral axis

## Warnings
- aspect_ratio=13.5 is outside the typical GA single-engine range [6, 10] (Raymer 2ed, Table 4.1 (p. 51))
- Web shear buckling sets the web thickness at 14 of 21 stations
